title: The One Who Ascended
text: No grave bears your name, because no body was left to bury. On clear nights, cultivators point at one particular star and argue about whether it was always there.

title: The Blood Demon
text: Mothers will use your name to frighten children for three hundred years. Where you died, nothing grows.

title: The Demon Who Made Peace
text: You inherited an army of monsters and left behind a sect of farmers and scholars. Historians will never agree on what you were. You would have liked that.

title: The Heavenly Demon
text: Ten thousand cultists wail at your funeral pyre. The righteous sects hold a quiet festival. The throne of skulls has one more.

title: The Hollow Hero
text: Your statue stands in the capital, noble and tall. Those who actually knew you spit as they pass it. Both groups are right.

title: Pillar of the Murim
text: Under your white banner the martial world knew a generation of peace. Every sect sends a sword to be buried with you. There is not room for them all.

title: Half Saint, Half Demon
text: The villages you saved build you shrines. The villages you burned build nothing at all. The storytellers need two voices to tell your tale.

title: A Legend of the Murim
text: A thousand years from now, a child will swing a wooden sword behind a barn and pretend to be you. That is what a legend is.

title: Calamity of the Age
text: It took the united strength of the martial world to outlive you, and they mostly did it by waiting. Your era has a name in the histories: the Dark Years.

title: The Greatest Scumbag Under Heaven
text: The day you die is declared a public holiday in three provinces. A latrine in the capital is named in your honour. It is, to be fair, a very famous latrine.

title: Hero of the Great War
text: You ended the war with one stroke on the Plain of Ten Thousand Graves. Old soldiers drink to you every year until there are no old soldiers left.

title: The One Who Ended the Righteous
text: The white banner fell by your hand, and an age fell with it. Even your own side feared to stand too near your grave.

title: Venerable Sect Leader
text: Your portrait hangs in the ancestral hall between the founder and an empty space for whoever comes next. Disciples bow to it each morning, and a few even mean it.

title: Lord of the Black Sky
text: The sect you built from outcasts and killers tears itself apart within a year of your death. It was only ever held together by fear of you.

title: The Righteous Outlaw
text: The magistrates called you a bandit. The poor called you something else. Offerings still appear at the foot of your mountain.

title: The Jackal
text: Too cruel to be laughed at, too shameless to be respected even as a villain. Other villains used your name as an insult.

title: A Great Hero
text: Not the greatest sword of your age, but the one people remember when they need courage. Your grave is never without fresh wine.

title: A Feared Villain
text: People check twice that you are really dead. Then they check a third time.

title: A Shameless Scoundrel
text: Your funeral is well attended, mostly by people confirming the news and trying to collect debts. The eulogy is short. Several mourners heckle.

title: The Rich Old Fox
text: You could not take it with you, though you certainly tried. Your heirs are still fighting over the will.

title: The Divine Doctor
text: You took more lives out of death's hands than any swordsman ever put into them. Patients you never met burn incense for you.

title: The Hidden Dragon
text: One of the strongest who ever lived, and almost nobody knew. The old sweeper at the temple gate, they called you. You preferred it that way.

title: A Sprout Cut Short
text: The martial world eats its young. Yours is one of ten thousand stories that ended in the first chapter.

title: The Sage of the Mountain
text: The hut above the clouds is empty now. Travellers say that if you sit there at dawn, the wind still sounds like someone sweeping leaves.

title: A Local Terror
text: A minor villain in a major world. A few villages sleep easier. Nobody else notices.

title: A Petty Rogue
text: You cheated your way through life and, in the end, life cheated you back. It seems fair.

title: A Quiet Life
text: No ballads, no statues. A warm house, a hand to hold at the end, and a child who has your stubborn chin. The murim would call it a small life. The murim is wrong.

title: A Local Hero
text: The wider world never learned your name, but one small town tells stories about you, and gets most of them right.

title: A Nameless Grave
text: One of ten thousand who entered the murim and left no mark. The grass does not care. It grows over heroes and nobodies alike.
